Task title: Rate limiter boundary and per-user state
Function entrypoint: allow_request

Product ticket:
# Product ticket: request rate limiter

## Background
The API should track recent requests and block excessive traffic.

## Happy path
- First normal requests are allowed.
- Request state is updated when a request is allowed.

## Policy note
The intended quota is five requests per rolling minute.

## Acceptance criteria
- First request is allowed.
- State stores allowed request timestamps.

Retrieved policy card:
Policy card ID: rate.limit.sixth_blocked
Title: The first request over the limit must be blocked
Requirement: The 6th request inside a 60 second window must be blocked.
Why it matters: The limiter can appear implemented while allowing the first abusive request over the limit.
Audit questions:
- Does the spec explicitly block the 6th request?
Keywords:

public_spec:
Title: Rate limiter boundary and per-user state

Behavior requirements:
- The system must allow up to 5 requests per rolling 60-second window per user.
- The 6th request within any 60-second window must be blocked.
- Per-user state must record timestamps of allowed requests to enforce the rolling window.
- Timestamps used for the window must be stored in a per-user non-volatile or in-memory store with correct eviction policy to reflect a rolling window.
- First request is allowed and updates per-user state with its timestamp.

Edge cases:
- Requests at the boundary of the 60-second window should be considered in the current window; those exactly 60 seconds older than current time are not counted.
- Multiple users must have isolated per-user state; one user's activity must not affect another.
- Clock drift or time skew should not cause incorrect allowance/denial; use monotonic or NTP-corrected timestamps where possible.
- Handling of missing or corrupted per-user state should default to allowing the first request and initializing state.
- High-frequency bursts should be correctly throttled after the 5th allowed request within any rolling window.

Acceptance criteria:
- AC1: The very first request from a user is allowed.
- AC2: The system stores the timestamp of each allowed request per user.
- AC3: No more than 5 requests per user are allowed within any rolling 60-second window.
- AC4: The 6th or more requests within the same rolling 60-second window are blocked.
- AC5: Per-user state is correctly updated after each allowed request, and old timestamps older than 60 seconds are pruned.

Non-goals:
- Implementing a fixed 60-second window (non-rolling) is not required; the policy specifies a rolling window.
- Cross-user state sharing (global quotas) is not allowed; quotas are per-user.
- Guaranteed throughput beyond allowed requests is not required; the limiter may introduce latency on blocked requests.
- Persisting state across restarts is outside current scope unless specified.

Testable assertions:
- Given a new user, the first request is allowed.
- After 5 allowed requests within 60 seconds, a 6th request is blocked.
- Requests spaced beyond 60 seconds from their corresponding timestamps are counted in a new window and allowed up to five again.
- Per-user state contains a list of at most the timestamps of the last allowed requests within the rolling window, pruned as older timestamps fall outside the 60-second window.
- Blocking is strictly enforced for the 6th request within the window; identical timestamps or clock anomalies do not bypass the rule.
